messages:
alerts-bot: INCIDENT — Dedicated pool 'eu3-dedicated-b' saturated. streaming p99 spikes >5s, p95 ~1.2s, p99 5.2s. Queue depth 420, warmup backlog growing. Paging oncall. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/eu3/pools/xyz, logs: http://logs/redwood/trace/7950001234 :rotating_light:

kiran: I'm oncall, grabbing this. confirm which customers are hitting the pool?

chris: acme-chat and internal-staging show the biggest load. acme-chat session streams show repeated stalls at token 1024.

tess: quick check — KV cache miss rate spiked from 4% -> 68% after the burst, warmup times per new slot ~10–14s. looks like a cold-pool warmup wave + sudden fanout from a large customer.

kiran: ok. immediate mitigation steps: 1) scale pool +2 GPUs, 2) enable temporary model fallback for streaming tails, 3) prime KV cache for top customer prefixes. who can run scale?

chris: I can run the scale now. command I'll use: ```infractl pool scale --pool eu3-dedicated-b --add 2 --reason "hotburst warmup surge"```

tess: I'll push a routing change to send 20% of new streaming sessions for AcmeChat to 'gptq-small-compat' as a graceful degrade. snippet: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood/internal/route -d '{"pool":"eu3","selector":"tenant:acme-chat","fallback":"gptq-small-compat","weight":0.2}'```

kiran: also priming KV cache: I'll run the priming job targeted at acme-chat top prefixes. ```jobs/prime-kv --tenant acme-chat --pool eu3-dedicated-b --prefixes file://acme-top-100.txt```

support-eng: notifying Customer Success / SRE with a quick blurb: "AcmeChat may see streaming stalls / slow responses; mitigation underway (scaling + fallback). We'll follow up with timeline."

chris: scale command executed, infra reports two nodes provisioning. pool health shows warmup queue decreasing but new warmup tasks still coming in.

tess: routing change deployed. fallback routing active for 20% of new sessions. KV priming job started.

kiran: monitoring — queue depth dropping: 420 -> 190 -> 95 over the last 4m. p99 trending down from 5.2s -> 2.4s. still above SLO but improving.

jules: thanks. if metrics haven't recovered to SLO within 30m escalate to SRE lead and consider temporarily enabling heavier degradation (50% fallback) and prewarming additional slots.

chris: provisioning finished, new nodes joined pool and are finishing warmup. slots usable: +128.

tess: KV hit rate recovered to ~12%, streaming stalls reduced in traces. AcmeChat error rate from streaming 5xx -> 502s down 80%.

kiran: Customer impact: AcmeChat experienced degraded streaming (stalls) for ~11m window, ~3% of sessions affected. Support notified.

alerts-bot: Severity downgraded — p99 now 1.8s, queue depth 42. Continue monitoring for 15m, then close if stable.

chris: leaving notes: runbook followed (dedicated-capacity -> warmup surge playbook). actions: scaled +2, routing fallback 20%, KV priming job, customer notified.

kiran: I'll hand this to oncall rotation notes. If we see a repeat pattern, we should revisit autoscaler warmup policy and target pool headroom. filed follow-up ticket: https://tickets/redwood/INC-7950001234-autoscale-warmup-tuning

tess: agree — recommending: increase warm pool min slots during business hours, prewarm for top tenants, and evaluate faster priming strategies.

jules: marking this incident as mitigated. oncall handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
